findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects stored in the reports bucket (including the uploaded vendor roster) have no enforced default server-side encryption.

findings.issue_category: No explicit private ACL or public access block
findings.description: The bucket sets no acl and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy, so its exposure posture depends entirely on account-level defaults rather than an explicit private configuration. This is the only bucket in the file with no ACL declared at all.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted with no recoverable prior version, removing tamper evidence and integrity protection for archived report data.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial ledger data is stored without an enforced default encryption policy.
Versioning is not enabled on the financial ledger bucket, allowing irreversible overwrite or deletion of financial records and defeating integrity and recovery controls.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts (potentially embedding proprietary or training data) are stored without enforced default encryption.
The runbooks bucket, which commonly holds operational procedures and internal architecture detail or embedded credentials, has no default server-side encryption configured.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid canned ACL and appears to be a corrupted "log-delivery-write". The audit log bucket's access control is therefore unverified and non-private, and no public access block or bucket policy compensates.

force_destroy = true on the bucket that receives S3 access logs allows the whole audit trail to be purged with the bucket in a single destroy operation, and no object lock or MFA delete is configured, undermining tamper resistance of security logs.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing supplier contact data/PII) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so the object is stored unencrypted. The source file is also committed into the repository alongside the Terraform code.

The bucket name "${local.env_prefix.value}-reports-science" shares the "-reports" prefix with the reports_archive bucket; any IAM or bucket policy written with a wildcard such as "*-reports*" will unintentionally grant access across both data sets, weakening least-privilege separation between report data and model artifacts.
